full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: First Appeal No. 132 of 2000 and First Appeal No. 615 of 1999 arising out of the same judgment and decree dated 23.8.99 passed by the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj in Title Suit No. 45 of 1999. 

 Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 23.8.99 the plaintiff preferred First Appeal No. 132 of 2000 while the contesting defendant Government of Bangladesh preferred First Appeal No. 615 of 1999. Since both the appeals arise out of the same judgment, these appeals were heard analogously and are being disposed of by a single judgment. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned judgment dated 23.8.99 decreed the suit in part, allowing 37 days to the plaintiff to enjoy the benefit of collection of tolls after the expiry of the lease period on 19.4.99 without making any payment to the Government. 6. It is against the aforesaid judgment dated 23.8.99 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Munshigonj that the defendant Government preferred the appeal before this court. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff appellant in First Appeal No. 132 of 2000 submits that the learned Subordinate Judge was manifestly wrong in not decreasing the suit in full inasmuch as the claim of the plaintiff is virtually admitted by the contesting defendants. The learned Advocate further submits that regard being had to the admitted fact that the representation of the plaintiff for free enjoyment of the bridges for a further period of 45 days for the purpose of collection of tolls being under the active consideration of the authority concerned, the learned Subordinate Judge was wholly wrong in not decreeing the suit in full. 

 8. Mr. M. A. Quayem, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the Government respondent in First Appeal No. 132 of 2000 and defendant-appellant in First Appeal No. 615 of 1999, on the other hand, submits that in view of the admitted fact that the lease of the plaintiff duly expired on 19.4.99 and a grace period of 50 days following thereafter also duly expired on 9.6.99 and no further extension of time was ever granted to the plaintiff by any authority of the defendant Government, the plaintiff is evidently left with no semblance of right and interest in the matter of collection of tolls from the disputed bridges and as such the plaintiff has no locus stand to challenge the authority of the Government to arrange for the collection of tolls from the bridges in question in any way it likes and, consequently, the suit must fail for want of any cause of action. The learned Deputy Attorney General also submits that 50 days grace was given to the plaintiff out of sheer humanitarian considerations and that gave the plaintiff no vested right in any form whatsoever in claiming further concessions for free enjoyment of the concerned bridges for a period of 45 days or for any other period and consequently the learned Subordinate Judge was manifestly wrong in decreeing the suit in part on a totally wrong view of law and fact and as such the impugned judgment must be set aside in the interest of justice. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submits that in the face of clear stipulations made in the lease-agreement dated 20.4.98 in Ext. 1, the plaintiff is never entitled to any concession or compensation resulting from disruption of normal traffic due to hartals or political blockades, and the plaintiff having no legal right to claim concessions even after the grace period ending on 9.6.99, the learned Subordinate Judge was manifestly wrong in granting an unwanted bounty of 37 days to the plaintiff against the overwhelming weight of the evidence and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed as a whole. 

 9. The point for determination.  The only point for determination in the two appeals is whether the learned Subordinate Judge was justified in decreeing the suit in part. 

 18. From the discussion of the evidence, we are satisfied that the plaintiff has totally failed to prove its case. It is unfortunate that the learned Subordinate Judge left the field of fact and evidence and strayed into fiction in decreeing the suit in part by doling out 37 days for free collection of tolls from the 2 bridges without any legal basis whatsoever. The grace of 50 days granted to the plaintiff after the expiry of the lease on 19.4.99 was out and out an act of unwanted charity doled out by the authority of the Government and it did not and could not give the plaintiff any vested right to claim further concessions for free enjoyment of toll collection for the 2 bridges. What was out and out a charity, has been taken for a right by the plaintiff and this prompted the plaintiff to file the present suit on frivolous allegations. On the expiry of the lease on 19.4.99 and the grace period ending on 9.6.99, there is evidently no existence of the lease and, therefore, the question of cancellation of lease by the impugned letter dated 20.6.99 is totally redundant. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, we find that the plaintiff initiated the veracious proceedings for making illegal gains, being emboldened by the undue favour already shown to it by the Governmental functionaries only at the cost of the state. 

 20. For the reasons stated above, we hold that the learned Subordinate Judge was manifestly wrong in decreeing the suit in part on illegal and irrelevant considerations. The learned Subordinate Judge failed to properly apply his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record and passed the impugned judgment essentially on surmises and conjectures. The approach of the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Munshigonj is strongly deprecated. The submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellant in F.A. No. 132 of 2000 are found without any substance and the same are accordingly repelled while we find sufficient substance in the submissions made by the learned D.A.G. in F.A. No. 615 of 1999 (Government of Bangladesh Vs. Zahangir Alam) and these are accordingly sustained. 

 21. In the result, F.A. No. 132 of 2000 is dismissed and F.A. No. 615 of 1999 is allowed with costs all through and the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.8.99 passed by the learned 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshigonj in Title Suit No. 45 of 1999 decreeing the suit in part are set aside. Title Suit No. 45 of 1999 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge Munshigonj is hereby dismissed.
